facts.claim: The official guide identifies Relationships as Ch. 5 in Part 2 Tools and Techniques.
facts.mechanism: Because the tools section begins with trust, later feedback methods are built on relationship capacity.
facts.commonError: Starting the tools section with scripts and tactics.
facts.whyWrong: Scripts fail when trust is absent.

facts.claim: Ch. 5 prompts managers to name activities that keep them centered.
facts.mechanism: Since an uncentered manager reacts defensively, self-management protects the relationship.
facts.commonError: Treating composure as a private wellness issue only.

facts.claim: Ch. 5 asks about times a manager could not bring a best self to work.
facts.mechanism: Because self-awareness reveals predictable failure points, managers can design safeguards.
facts.commonError: Pretending leaders should always be unaffected.
facts.whyWrong: Unacknowledged strain leaks into management behavior.

facts.claim: Ch. 5 asks how trust is built with direct reports.
facts.mechanism: Because trust depends on repeated evidence, managers need observable practices rather than intentions.
facts.commonError: Assuming direct reports trust a boss by default.
facts.whyWrong: Power makes trust something to earn.

facts.claim: Order of Operations spans Ch. 5-6 and starts with soliciting feedback.
facts.mechanism: Because receiving first lowers hierarchy, the manager shows candor is reciprocal.
facts.commonError: Demanding openness from employees before inviting it upward.

facts.claim: The official phrase get before give summarizes the first relationship move.
facts.mechanism: Since the boss has more power, asking first makes later challenge less hypocritical.
facts.whyWrong: The manager has not yet shown willingness to hear hard truth.

facts.claim: Radical Candor LLC is described as a global executive education company founded by Kim Scott and Jason Rosoff.
facts.mechanism: Because the practices are taught organizationally, relationship routines must be repeatable.
facts.whyWrong: Repeatable routines make the tool teachable.

facts.claim: The official page says the work has been translated into 20 languages.
facts.mechanism: Because wide translation requires portable behaviors, the relationship advice should not depend on one office culture.
facts.commonError: Copying one Silicon Valley scene as universal.
facts.whyWrong: The portable mechanism is trust behavior.

facts.claim: Relationship work comes before Guidance, Team, and Results tools.
facts.mechanism: Because later tools create more pressure, trust must exist before conflict escalates.
facts.commonError: Trying to install candor only when performance problems appear.
facts.whyWrong: Crisis is a poor time to build the first trust signal.

allowedAnchors.label: trust routines
allowedAnchors.text: Relationship-building becomes practical when managers create repeatable routines for trust: staying centered, making time for real conversations, and showing that power is not the only thing moving the relationship. Tools for guidance and results fail when the relationship cannot carry them. Trust routines make future candor less surprising and less threatening.
